key_insight: Large tensor-network classical simulation via DMRG provides a strong benchmark showing current NISQ quantum methods struggle to match classical accuracy on the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick ground-state problem.
engineering_relevance: The results help quantum engineers choose and validate algorithms by quantifying how far VQE and SQD can scale on real hardware before noise and circuit depth dominate.
method: Ran DMRG on NERSC Perlmutter to generate high-accuracy LMG ground-state energies.
Compared against VQE and SQD executed on an IBM Eagle quantum computer.
Evaluated accuracy as particle count increased, focusing on ground-state energy error.
evidence_signal: The dataset covers systems up to 1400 particles, while VQE stayed within 1% error only at 6 particles and SQD extended that to 17 particles.
watch_item: Results are hardware- and noise-dependent, so performance on one IBM Eagle setup may not generalize to other devices, ansatz choices, or error-mitigation strategies.
paper_title: Benchmarking Quantum Simulations of the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick Model Using Large Tensor Networks
